newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece slashes tax breaks, sees intake of 130bln.
newsitem.headline: Greece slashes tax breaks, sees intake of 130bln.

text.p: Greece will do away with numerous tax exemptions to boost tax revenues by 130 billion drachmas in 1997, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou told reporters.

"It is the first time tax reform has such a strong element of social justice. The tax exemptions that will be abolished will affect social groups with above average incomes. This is the tone approved by the cabinet," he said.
Those hit hardest include flight crews in civil aviation, professional athletes, members of parliament and journalists.
This is part of an effort to cut its 1997 budget deficit to 4.2 percent of GDP from a 1996's expected 7.6 percent.
Greece wants to join European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) by 2000 or 2001 but has failed to meet a single target for doing so. Greece is the only EU country in that position.

Papandoniou has said he will present the toughest budget in 15 years later this week. It will be the first budget from Prime Minister Costas Simitis, who won elections in September. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
